title: Leon Marchand's New Olympic Dream: Freestyle
summary:
Leon Marchand is one of the greatest swimmers of his generation. At the 2024 Paris Olympics, he won four gold medals in the 200m and 400m individual medleys, the 200m butterfly, and the 200m breaststroke. But now, he's ready to close that chapter and open a new one.

"I have absolutely no desire to repeat myself," Marchand said. "It's done, so that chapter is closed." Instead, he's setting his sights on the freestyle events—specifically the 200m and 400m freestyle—for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

This shift came after a hip injury forced him to change his event lineup at the European Championships. He focused on freestyle and butterfly, and the results were eye-opening. He won both the 400m freestyle and 200m butterfly, with a blistering 3:43.14 in the 400 free—the fastest time in the field by nearly a second and a half. He also led off the 4x200 freestyle relay in 1:43.76, making him the 7th-fastest performer in history.

"I think I've found my thing!" Marchand exclaimed. "I really want to continue this momentum in the freestyle." He attributes his improvement to two years of hard work on technique, power, and his kick. "This is a bit of a reward for what I've been doing for two years."

Marchand acknowledges that his freestyle times aren't the best in the world yet, but he's driven by the challenge. "I want to do that for Los Angeles, why not... The 200 freestyle, why not, the 400 freestyle... I'll see how it goes." He's also mindful of his adductor injury and will monitor how his body responds.

It's a bold move from a swimmer who could easily rest on his laurels. But Marchand thrives on new challenges. If his European Championships performance is any indication, the freestyle events at the LA Olympics could be his next masterpiece.
why_it_matters: Marchand's gamble will help shape the freestyle rivalry at the 2028 Olympics, and it shows that a top athlete can choose a harder path instead of repeating old successes.

background_read: Leon Marchand is a French swimmer who became an international star at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he won four gold medals and was one of the faces of those Games.
The individual medley is one of swimming's toughest events because it requires all four strokes: butterfly, backstroke, breaststroke, and freestyle.
The European Championships are a major continental competition, one level below the world championships and the Olympics, so swimmers often use them to test new events.
Marchand is now aiming at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where the freestyle events will be among the most competitive races in the pool.
The 400m freestyle is a test of endurance and pacing, while the 200m version demands speed and sustained power.
At the elite level, swimmers sometimes switch events late in their careers to protect their bodies or find fresh motivation, and Marchand's move from medley to freestyle follows that pattern.

perspectives.description: Fans get to watch one of swimming's biggest stars try a new challenge, and Marchand's early freestyle times suggest he could become a medal contender in two events.
Leaving the individual medley means giving up events he is already great at. A single injury could derail the freestyle plan, and the 400m free field is brutally strong.
Swimmers often change event focus with age or injuries, so this is a natural evolution rather than a shock. The European Championships gave him a controlled test, but Olympic level is another step.
If his body holds up and his kick keeps improving, Marchand could enter the LA Games with some of the fastest freestyle times in the world, creating a major duel with the current freestyle stars.
